title: Make rules-pack audit CLI tests deterministic under suite load
description: The full Vitest suite intermittently times out packages/core/test/rulesPackAuditCli.test.ts at the fixed 5s default because each test cold-starts the TypeScript CLI subprocess. Observed on 2026-07-14: the strict-audit case took 5.28-6.86s under 4-6 forks and timed out, while the entire file passed alone and the suite passed with one fork. Investigate and remove the load-sensitive cold-start behavior (for example, a testable in-process command boundary or reusable compiled entrypoint) rather than raising the global timeout or merely reducing CI parallelism. If a narrow per-test timeout remains necessary after root-cause work, document why. Also assess the same subprocess pattern in importer/audit CLI tests so the deterministic fix is shared where appropriate.
acceptance_criteria: Full default-parallel npm test runs repeatedly without rulesPackAuditCli timeout failures under representative load; solution does not raise Vitest's global timeout or weaken assertions; focused rulesPackAuditCli tests remain green; design/root-cause rationale is documented in the bead/PR.
notes:
Additional 2026-07-14 evidence during PR #451 review: even VITEST_MAX_FORKS=1 full verification timed out the unchanged human-report and --json cases at 5.66s and 5.72s, while prior isolated runs passed. This rules out Vitest fork contention as a complete solution and reinforces removing/reusing the tsx subprocess cold-start boundary.
Dispatch plan (attempt 1, 2026-07-19, supervisor eshyra-fe3t): Codex gpt-5.6-luna in .worktrees/eshyra-stbg branch eshyra-stbg off eshyra-fe3t (=main 9d252b9). Approach guidance: replace per-test tsx CLI subprocess cold-starts with a testable in-process command boundary (export a run function from the CLI module; keep a thin argv shim); keep CLI-contract coverage via at most one true subprocess smoke test; do not raise global timeouts or weaken assertions; assess the same pattern in other importer/audit CLI tests and share the fix where cheap.
Completion report (2026-07-19): Replaced repeated tsx subprocess execution in rulesPackAuditCli.test.ts with an exported in-process runCli(argv, io) boundary. The thin CLI entrypoint now adapts argv/process streams and preserves fail-closed exit codes: 0 success, 1 strict findings/changes, 2 load/validation failure. Tests retain human/JSON, strict audit/diff, invalid-pack, help, and root npm-script wiring assertions without changing global timeout or weakening expectations. Assessed all test-side importer/audit subprocess patterns: only rulesPackAuditCli used the repeated tsx cold-start pattern; installer/release/Unicode tests are unrelated platform/integration subprocess checks. Focused suite: 10/10 passed. Typecheck, direct CLI help, format, and biome ci passed. Required npm run verify:worktree was attempted but blocked by managed sandbox spawnSync git EPERM in check:hidden-unicode; full npm test had 4,616 passing, 4 skipped files, with 23 unrelated child-process/network permission failures under the same sandbox. No follow-up bead discovered.
